faqs.a: For a lump sum with no payments: rate = (FV/PV)^(1/years) - 1. With payments, there is no closed formula, so this calculator solves the full TVM equation numerically with bisection search.
faqs.q: How is the interest rate calculated?

faqs.a: Annual compounding applies the rate once per year; monthly compounding applies one-twelfth of the rate each month, which grows slightly faster. With monthly payments selected, monthly mode matches how most savings plans actually work.
It solves the same equation for the rate with PV set to 0, your monthly payment, and your target. For example, $500/month for 20 years to reach $500,000 needs about 7.55% annual.
faqs.q: Can I find the rate for a savings plan?

faqs.a: The Rule of 72: divide 72 by the rate to estimate doubling years. At 7.18%, money doubles in about 10 years. The calculator shows this estimate live under your answer.

That means the goal is impossible at those inputs with a constant rate - for example a future value below the present value with no payments would need a negative rate, or the target is unreachable even at 200% per period.
faqs.q: Why does it say no solution?

faqs.a: Nominal APR (monthly rate x 12) is what lenders and plans usually quote; effective annual rate ((1 + monthly)^12 - 1) is slightly higher. At small rates the difference is tiny; this calculator reports the nominal APR.

interest-rate-calculator.formula:
FV = PV x (1+r)^n + PMT x ((1+r)^n - 1)/r
With PMT = 0: r = (FV/PV)^(1/n) - 1
With payments, r is solved numerically (bisection) from the same equation.
Rule of 72: doubling years ~ 72 / annual rate %.

interest-rate-calculator.quickAnswer: To grow $10,000 into $20,000 in 10 years with annual compounding and no payments, you need a rate of 7.18% per year: (20,000/10,000)^(1/10) - 1. At that rate, money doubles every 10 years by the Rule of 72 (72 / 7.18 = 10.03).
interest-rate-calculator.tagline: Solve for the rate your lump sum or savings plan needs.
interest-rate-calculator.workedExample:
$10,000 to $20,000, 10 years, annual compounding, no payments:
1. Formula: r = (FV/PV)^(1/n) - 1.
2. r = (20,000/10,000)^(1/10) - 1 = 2^0.1 - 1.
3. 2^0.1 = about 1.071773, so r = about 7.18% per year.
4. Check: $10,000 x 1.071773^10 = $10,000 x 2.0 = $20,000. Matches.
5. Doubling years = 72 / 7.18 = about 10.0 years.
